item.title: As Germany's Merz feels the pressure, an ally seeks to avoid leadership talk
item.description: Hendrik Wuest, the German state premier often seen as a possible replacement for struggling Chancellor Friedrich Merz, dismisses the leadership talk but his profile has risen as the ruling conservatives deal with their worst-ever election loss.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Rinke
item.content:encoded: Hendrik Wuest, the German state premier often seen as a possible replacement for struggling Chancellor Friedrich Merz, dismisses the leadership talk but his profile has risen as the ruling conservatives deal with their [USN:L1N45C01D TEXT:"worst-ever election"] loss. This week, only days after the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) topped a state election for the second time in two weeks, Wuest took a business delegation on a three-day visit to Turkey, where he met President Tayyip Erdogan. Foreign visits by the premiers of large German states are relatively common and Wuest's state of North Rhine-Westphalia has been home to Germany's largest Turkish population since the first Turks arrived as "guest workers" in Germany in the 1960s. But the timing of the trip, underlining Wuest's status as a major player in German politics while Merz was fighting for his [USN:L8N45C0DZ TEXT:"political life"] and strains in the coalition have re-emerged, fuelled speculation about a possible change of chancellor. Wuest and officials who work with him have repeatedly denied he has any interest in replacing Merz under current circumstances. He was one of eight conservative state premiers who publicly backed the chancellor in the run-up to the September 20 election in the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, where the AfD again topped the election after winning in Saxony-Anhalt two weeks earlier. However, the results underlined how far voters have turned against Merz, who vowed to carry on despite the worst defeat ever inflicted on his Christian Democrats (CDU), who failed to pass the threshold to enter parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Widely blamed for failing to deliver on promised economic reforms and hampered by a series of communications missteps that have contributed to perceptions of being out of touch with worries over eroding living standards, the chancellor's approval ratings have fallen to record lows. An opinion poll this week by the Forsa polling institute showed only 11% approved of the job he was doing and even among his own party supporters, only 39% were satisfied. Wuest, by contrast, is the third most popular politician in the country behind Social Democrat (SPD) Defence Minister Boris Pistorius and Baden-Wuerttemberg state premier Cem Ozdemir, from the Greens, according to ilium, a data analysis service. UNDER SCRUTINY Germany's constitutional system does not make it easy to replace a sitting chancellor. Any change would also not solve deep-seated problems, ranging from an ageing population and war on its doorstep in Ukraine to the erosion of its industrial base which has been fast losing ground to China. "The problems — like having to push through unpopular austerity measures in the social security systems with a difficult coalition partner, the SPD, which is also feeling uncertain — would still be there," said one senior CDU politician. Opinion polls suggest Wuest, whose state goes to the polls next April, could retain power with his Green coalition partners, potentially putting him in position to take the conservatives into the next federal election due in 2029. He has struck a markedly different tone from the instinctively pro-business, fiscal conservative Merz who has himself admitted widespread perceptions that his party did not appear to care enough about "social justice". Wuest has previously criticised the government's messaging on economic reforms, which several senior figures in the party see as excessively technocratic. "It is not enough simply to keep talking about the need to push through the agreed reforms, as some members of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group and the Chancellor emphasise," said another conservative state premier. At a time when the success of the AfD has fed alarm among many people with a migrant background and led to a tougher stance on immigration from the government, Wuest made a clear break with the AfD's anti-immigrant rhetoric and said it was inadmissible to allow anyone to feel personally threatened. "This makes our task as a society to combat this resentment and discrimination all the more important," he said. While supporting the idea that refugees from war-torn countries like Syria could normally return to their countries once peace returned, he noted the positive contribution of workers from countries like Turkey at a time when Germany has sought to attract skilled workers. "We'll manage to make the distinction," he said.

item.title: Supreme Court to weigh Trump's mandatory immigration detention policy
item.description: The US Supreme Court agreed on Thursday to hear a dispute over a policy by President Donald Trump's administration that subjects millions of immigrants in the United States illegally to mandatory detention during their deportation proceedings.
item.dc:creator: John Kruzel
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court agreed on Thursday to hear a dispute over a policy by President Donald Trump 's administration that subjects millions of immigrants in the United States illegally to mandatory detention during their deportation proceedings. In this latest legal battle over Trump's hardline immigration agenda to reach the top US judicial body, the justices face an issue that has divided lower courts as numerous lawsuits by migrants and advocacy groups challenging the policy have played out. The policy is one of a number of measures his administration has taken in its pursuit of Trump's goal of mass deportation. The justices took up the administration's appeal of a ruling against the policy by the New York-based 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals in a case involving a Brazilian national. The Supreme Court will hear the case in its new term that begins on Monday. The US Department of Homeland Security in July 2025 issued new guidance to federal immigration officials announcing that immigrants in the United States illegally are subject to mandatory detention without a bond hearing for the duration of their deportation proceedings, which can take months or even years to play out. The guidance represented a departure from a nearly three-decade-old interpretation of federal law that immigrants already living in the United States could be released on bond while they pursue their cases in immigration court. The Republican president has enforced a sweeping crackdown on immigration — among his top priorities — since returning to office last year. The Supreme Court, which has a 6-3 conservative majority, has allowed a number of Trump's hardline immigration policies to go into effect. Immigrants detained under the policy have filed tens of thousands of lawsuits seeking their release. A Reuters analysis in February [USN:L6N3Z714G TEXT:"found"] that hundreds of judges around the country had ruled more than 4,400 times that Trump's administration had detained such immigrants unlawfully. The 2nd Circuit decision arose from a legal challenge brought by Ricardo Aparecido Barbosa da Cunha, who entered the United States illegally around 2004 or 2005 and has remained since then. He was arrested by immigration officers in September 2025 while driving to work in Norwood, Massachusetts, and initially was denied a bond hearing under the disputed policy. He was subsequently released on bond at a later stage of his case, according to court papers. SPLIT AMONG APPEALS COURTS The voluminous litigation has led to a split among federal appellate courts. For instance, the New Orleans-based 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals in a 2-1 decision in February sided with Trump. In a decision reversing rulings that had led to the release of two Mexican men, US Circuit Judge Edith Jones wrote that decisions by prior administrations not to use mandatory detention, as Trump is doing, do not mean "they lacked the authority to do more." Most federal appellate courts to review the policy have ruled against it. Decisions against the policy by the 2nd Circuit and Cincinnati-based 6th US Circuit Court of Appeals prompted the administration to appeal to the Supreme Court. The court already is set to hear arguments in another major immigration-related case during its term. The court on Tuesday let the administration resume, for now, swiftly deporting migrants to countries other than their own without offering them the chance to show the harms they may face. The justices scheduled arguments in that case for December.

item.title: Schmid diz que avaliar impacto do choque energético é grande desafio para o Fed
item.description: Avaliar o impacto dos altos preços da energia sobre a inflação continua sendo um desafio para os responsáveis pela política monetária dos EUA, que tentam determinar se a inflação atual é persistente, afirmou nesta quinta-feira o presidente do Federal Reserve de Kansas City, Jeff Schmid.
item.dc:creator: Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: Avaliar o impacto dos altos preços da energia sobre a inflação continua sendo um desafio para os responsáveis pela política monetária dos EUA, que tentam determinar se a inflação atual é persistente, afirmou nesta quinta-feira o presidente do Federal Reserve de Kansas City, Jeff Schmid. “Provavelmente, esse é um dos maiores desafios para a política monetária atualmente -- o que está por trás desse tipo de choque de oferta” e por quanto tempo ele poderá persistir e se refletir na inflação, disse Schmid em uma conferência do Fed de Richmond sobre desenvolvimento rural.

item.title: ICC cuts ties with AXA over US sanctions, FT reports
item.description: The International Criminal Court has cut ties with its health insurance provider Axa in a bid to shield itself from US sanctions, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The International Criminal Court has cut ties with its health insurance provider Axa (AXAF.PA) in a bid to shield itself from US sanctions, the Financial Times reported on Thursday. A spokesperson for the ICC told the paper Axa and the court had “decided by mutual agreement to terminate the contractual relationship” and that it would use a new, unnamed health insurance provider. Axa was quoted in the FT as saying: “It is a complex and sensitive case given the risks arising from the extraterritorial application of US sanctions. Situations of this kind, which are extremely difficult for the individuals affected, are relatively new and reflect an international environment that has become increasingly tense and complex for businesses.”

item.title: Renee Good's family sues Trump administration over fatal Minneapolis shooting
item.description: The family of Renee Good, one of two US citizens fatally shot by federal immigration agents in Minneapolis in January, sued US President Donald Trump's administration on Thursday over her killing during deportation sweeps.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Allen
item.content:encoded: The family of Renee Good, one of two US citizens fatally shot by federal immigration agents in Minneapolis in January, sued US President Donald Trump's administration on Thursday over her killing during deportation sweeps. Good, 37, was shot dead in her car by a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent on January 7, when she and her wife joined one of the city's daily protests against masked and armed federal agents deployed to Minnesota to arrest migrants for deportation. The two lawsuits say Trump administration officials were negligent and violated the civil rights of Good and others in Minneapolis, demanding a jury trial and damages. They are among the first major civil actions taken against Trump for his unprecedented deportation sweeps in Minneapolis last winter, dubbed Operation Metro Surge. Good's killing intensified the backlash in Minnesota and beyond against the sweeps, involving thousands of immigration agents deployed to street patrols in Minnesota. Trump ended the Minnesota surge in February, but says his anti-immigration policies are needed for the safety of native-born Americans. Days after Good's death, an ICE agent shot and wounded Julio Sosa-Celis, a Venezuelan delivery driver, in the leg, and two weeks later immigration agents fatally shot Alex Pretti, an American nurse working for the US Department of Veterans Affairs. Senior Trump administration officials initially branded Good a "domestic terrorist" and the US Department of Justice stopped its federal prosecutors in Minneapolis from investigating the agents involved in her killing, prompting at least half a dozen of those prosecutors to resign in protest. None of the agents involved has yet faced any charges. Good's killing was captured on widely viewed videos that showed the ICE agent, Jonathan Ross, approaching Good in her car, which was parked to partly block the road. Ross circled her car on foot, recording on his cellphone. In her last words, Good can be seen on video saying to Ross: "That's fine, dude, I'm not mad at you." Moments later, another ICE agent approached the car and told Good to get out. She can be seen reversing briefly, then putting the car into forward gear and turning the steering wheel to her right, apparently trying to drive away. As the car moves forward, Ross, who at that point had returned to the front left of her car, shouts "Whoa!" and shoots into the car, hitting Good three times: in the head, in her arm and in her torso. Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty, the chief elected prosecutor in Minneapolis, is investigating the agents who killed Good and Pretti for possible violations of Minnesota law. The investigations have been slowed because the Justice Department withdrew its usual cooperation and evidence-sharing with local law enforcement agencies. Minnesota has sued the Trump administration to gain access to the evidence it gathered at the shooting scenes. Ross has not publicly discussed Good's death or his actions that day, and he could not immediately be reached for comment on Thursday. The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE and related agencies, has defended the conduct of Ross and other immigration officers as justified uses of force in dangerous situations. Good's wife, Becca Good, and other relatives are due to speak to reporters about their lawsuits later on Thursday morning.

item.title: Funcionário do MSF testa positivo para Ebola no Congo, diz organização humanitária
item.description: Um funcionário da organização humanitária Médicos Sem Fronteiras (MSF) testou positivo para o vírus Ebola Bundibugyo enquanto trabalhava na resposta à epidemia de Ebola na República Democrática do Congo, informou o MSF nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Um funcionário da organização humanitária Médicos Sem Fronteiras (MSF) testou positivo para o vírus Ebola Bundibugyo enquanto trabalhava na resposta à epidemia de Ebola na República Democrática do Congo, informou o MSF nesta quinta-feira. “Essa pessoa está sendo retirada com segurança, seguindo um protocolo médico rigoroso e em estreita coordenação com as autoridades de saúde competentes na RDC e na Holanda, onde o paciente será recebido por um hospital designado”, informou o MSF em comunicado. O número de casos confirmados de Ebola no Congo ultrapassou 8.000 pela primeira vez desde o início do surto em curso no país da África Central, segundo dados do governo divulgados na segunda-feira. O último relatório de situação do instituto de saúde pública estimou o número de casos em 8.067 e de mortes em 3.901. O surto, causado pela cepa Bundibugyo do Ebola, tornou-se o maior e mais mortal da história do Congo, superando a epidemia de 2018-2020. Ele fica atrás apenas do surto da África Ocidental de 2014-2016, que infectou mais de 28.600 pessoas e matou mais de 11.000 na Guiné, na Libéria e em Serra Leoa. O MSF, que está atuando no surto nas províncias de Ituri, Kivu do Norte, Tshopo e Haut-Uélé, afirmou reconhecer que, apesar de fornecer à equipe os mais altos níveis possíveis de proteção, o risco de exposição nunca pode ser completamente eliminado.

item.title: Flydubai by the numbers after incident on Israel-bound flight
item.description: Dubai state-owned airline flydubai is in the headlines after a co-pilot on an Israel-bound flight stabbed the pilot before being constrained by passengers, allowing reserve pilots on the plane to safely land the aircraft in Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Federico Maccioni, Joanna Plucinska
item.content:encoded: Dubai state-owned airline flydubai is in the headlines after a co-pilot on an Israel-bound flight stabbed the pilot before being constrained by passengers, allowing reserve pilots on the plane to safely land the aircraft in Saudi Arabia. Israel has [USN:L6N45N0LN TEXT:"vowed to find out"] what was behind the attack. Here are some facts about the airline. FLEET SIZE Flydubai has a fleet of 98 Boeing 737 aircraft, which includes 25 next-generation Boeing 737-800, 69 Boeing 737 MAX 8 jets and four Boeing 737 MAX 9 aircraft, it says. It is also a major buyer. In November last year it agreed to buy 150 Airbus A321neo planes to be delivered from 2031 and valued at $24 billion, with options for a further 100 of the aircraft. In addition, it has signed a $13 billion deal for 75 737 MAXs, with options for 75 more aircraft. ROUTES Flydubai says that it flies to over 125 destinations in some 56 countries across Africa, Europe, Central Asia, the Gulf, the Middle East, the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. STAFF The state-backed carrier has over 6,000 employees from 144 countries. While the airline doesn't break down pilot numbers, it said in 2024 that it was on a recruitment drive to hire 130 new pilots by the end of that year. According to its careers website, captains have a basic monthly salary with housing and transport allowance of 50,235 United Arab Emirates dirhams ($13,677). FINANCIALS AND BUSINESS PERFORMANCE The carrier transported 15.7 million passengers in 2025, a 2% increase from a year before, bringing in revenue of around $3.7 billion and after-tax profits of $531 million, the firm said in its latest annual report. ($1 = 3.6729 UAE dirham)

item.title: Trump dice que lamenta haber nombrado a los jueces de la Corte Suprema Gorsuch, Barrett y Kavanaugh
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó que lamentaba haber nombrado a tres magistrados de la Corte Suprema -Neil Gorsuch, Amy Coney Barrett y Brett Kavanaugh- que se han opuesto a él en sentencias recientes, según una entrevista concedida a la revista Time.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó que lamentaba haber nombrado a tres magistrados de la Corte Suprema -Neil Gorsuch, Amy Coney Barrett y Brett Kavanaugh- que se han opuesto a él en sentencias recientes, según una entrevista concedida a la revista Time. En la entrevista, realizada el lunes, se le preguntó al mandatario republicano por sus recientes comentarios sobre los tres magistrados conservadores. "¿Se arrepiente de haberlos nombrado?", preguntó el entrevistador, refiriéndose a los comentarios de Trump en una reciente publicación en su plataforma Truth Social. "Sí. Sí", respondió Trump, según la transcripción de la entrevista. "¿Qué puedo hacer? Yo los nombré. Han votado en mi contra demasiadas veces. Estaba muy (...) Les di el puesto de su vida y votan en mi contra a menudo". Trump nombró a Gorsuch, Kavanaugh y Barrett durante su primer mandato, creando así una mayoría conservadora de 6 a 3 y permitiendo que la Corte Suprema tomara un giro drástico hacia la derecha desde 2020. "Sí, me gusta la lealtad, sí", dijo Trump al entrevistador, quien a continuación le preguntó si eso era lo que esperaba de los magistrados. "No, no quiero lealtad. Quiero buenas decisiones", respondió. Después de que el máximo órgano judicial del país rechazara una norma del Servicio Postal que restringía el uso de las papeletas por correo en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura de noviembre, Trump afirmó que sus designados se estaban comportando de forma diferente a como lo habían hecho durante las entrevistas. "Estas no son las personas a las que entrevisté para formar parte de la Corte Suprema de Estados Unidos; son meramente una sombra de lo que eran", escribió en Truth Social. Después de que la Corte Suprema anulara en febrero sus amplios aranceles globales, al considerar que los había impuesto ilegalmente utilizando una ley destinada a emergencias nacionales, Trump reservó su ira especialmente para Gorsuch y Barrett, quienes formaron parte de la mayoría en ese fallo de 6 a 3.

item.title: Canadian factory PMI hits six-month low in September on trade frictions
item.description: Canada's manufacturing sector expanded at the slowest pace in six months in September as trade frictions and elevated energy prices weighed on activity, while confidence in the outlook dropped to the lowest level in nine months.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: Canada's manufacturing sector expanded at the slowest pace in six months in September as trade frictions and elevated energy prices weighed on activity, while confidence in the outlook dropped to the lowest level in nine months. The S&P Global Canada Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to 51.5 last month from 53.0 in August, marking the lowest level since March. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the sector. “Canada’s manufacturing economy showed a degree of resilience in the face of several headwinds during September," Paul Smith, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said in a statement. “However, tariffs and elevated global energy prices due to the war in Iran continued to have a damaging impact on the sector." A [USN:L6N45H0RX TEXT:"US import ban"] on many Canadian alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and dairy products took effect on Tuesday after talks involving President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Mark Carney broke down in August. The output index dipped to 50.8 from 52.8 in August, while the new orders measure slipped below the 50 threshold for the first time since March. “These issues didn’t just cause present difficulties, such as around stock and production management, but also added to a pervading uncertainty amongst clients and manufacturers alike especially given the seemingly intractable nature of trade tensions with the US and the ongoing conflict in the Middle East," Smith said. The future output index fell to its lowest level since December 2025 at 54.6, down from 58.7 in August, while delivery delays grew the most widespread since August 2022 and inflation pressures intensified. The measure of input costs rose to 71.1 from 66.4 in August, notching its highest level since July 2022.

item.title: Second Hull player involved in car accident on same road 20 days later
item.description: Hull City's French midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath was involved in a car accident on Thursday, The Telegraph reported, on the same road as one involving teammate Sorba Thomas 20 days before.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hull City's French midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath was involved in a car accident on Thursday, The Telegraph reported, on the same road as one involving teammate Sorba Thomas 20 days before. Both incidents took place on Millhouse Woods Lane, the road that leads to Hull's training ground. The road has a speed limit of 30 mph (48 kph). Humberside Police said police and emergency services attended a traffic collision on Thursday involving a single vehicle at 8:30 a.m. and there were no injuries. The 23-year-old Gourna-Douath's car was on its side after the accident, The Telegraph said. Hull's Wales winger Thomas, 27, emerged "completely unscathed" after an [USN:L4N4530VE TEXT:"accident on September 11"], with images showing his car upside down on a small residential road. Reuters has contacted Hull for comment. The promoted side have had an encouraging start to the season and stand in eighth place in the Premier League. They next host Everton on October 11.

item.title: Sudan's ousted president Bashir sent to Khartoum for treatment, lawyer says
item.description: Ousted Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir has been transferred to a military-run hospital in Khartoum for medical treatment and requires further care outside the country, his lawyer said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Khalid Abdelaziz
item.content:encoded: Ousted Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir has been transferred to a military-run hospital in Khartoum for medical treatment and requires further care outside the country, his lawyer said on Thursday. Bashir, 82, was toppled by the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in April 2019, following a months-long popular uprising. The RSF and army later fell out over plans to integrate their forces during a planned transition to civilian rule and have been fighting a civil war that has [USN:L6N45M0KU TEXT:"laid waste"] to much of the country over the past three-and-a-half years. Bashir had been moved from prison to hospital prior to the outbreak of war, and [USN:C6N325021 TEXT:"later transferred"] to the town of Merowe in northern Sudan, where he had been put under military guard. Bashir was sent to Khartoum for medical tests and he had symptoms that required diagnosis and treatment outside Sudan, his lawyer, Mohamed Alhassan Alameen, told Reuters. In a statement on Wednesday, Bashir's family said his need for medical treatment outside Sudan "has become critical and urgent, and cannot be delayed any longer", but they had not received official permission to send him abroad. It was unclear precisely what condition Bashir was suffering. Sudan's military did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Several prominent [USN:L1N3TM0V6 TEXT:"Sudanese Islamist figures"] also called for his transfer out of the country on social media. Any such move would likely cause discord within Sudan and could draw international condemnation since [USN:L6N3VN0KH TEXT:"Bashir is wanted"] by the International Criminal Court on charges including genocide and also has open cases against him in Sudan. During Bashir's three decades in power, Sudan was listed by the US as a state sponsor of terrorism and was subject to wide-ranging sanctions. Protesters during the popular uprising accused him and his Islamist National Congress Party of widespread corruption and repression. After his ouster, Bashir was tried on various charges and convicted of corruption and illicit financing, for which he was serving prison time at the start of the war.

item.title: Hackers chinos se hicieron pasar por exfuncionaria de EEUU para robar correos electrónicos sobre IA
item.description: Unos hackers chinos se hicieron pasar por expertos estadounidenses en inteligencia artificial, entre ellos una antigua funcionaria del Gobierno, para intentar robar correos electrónicos a expertos de centros de estudios, universidades y otras organizaciones, según informó el jueves la empresa de ciberseguridad Proofpoint.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter, A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: Unos hackers chinos se hicieron pasar por expertos estadounidenses en inteligencia artificial, entre ellos una antigua funcionaria del Gobierno, para intentar robar correos electrónicos a expertos de centros de estudios, universidades y otras organizaciones, según informó el jueves la empresa de ciberseguridad Proofpoint. En un informe, Proofpoint señaló que había observado cómo los hackers —a los que denomina "TA419"— intentan robar contraseñas de forma regular a personas que trabajan para centros de estudios, empresas de defensa, universidades y bufetes de abogados de Estados Unidos o Japón desde el año 2025. Proofpoint atribuyó estos ataques al grupo chino basándose en los tipos de malware utilizados, la infraestructura de Internet empleada para llevar a cabo los ataques y los objetivos en los que observó que se centraba el grupo, que coinciden con las prioridades de recopilación de información de los servicios de inteligencia chinos. Proofpoint señaló que la reciente campaña de los hackers consistía en redactar correos electrónicos que fingían proceder de expertos en IA o en asuntos de Estado, entre ellos Lynne Parker, quien anteriormente trabajó como subdirectora principal de la Oficina de Política Científica y Tecnológica de la Casa Blanca. Proofpoint indicó que los correos electrónicos solían proponer colaboraciones o iniciativas relacionadas con la IA antes de dirigir a los destinatarios hacia sitios web destinados a robar contraseñas. La embajada china en Washington no respondió de inmediato a un mensaje en el que se le solicitaban comentarios. Pekín lleva mucho tiempo negando que lleve a cabo operaciones de ciberespionaje. Proofpoint se negó a revelar los nombres de los objetivos de los piratas informáticos, limitándose a indicar que entre ellos se encontraban "expertos que trabajan en la regulación de la IA, los controles de exportación y la estrategia nacional de IA". Reuters pudo identificar de forma independiente a uno de ellos: Alex Engler, un exfuncionario de la Casa Blanca que ahora dirige el Penn Center on Media, Technology, and Democracy. Engler dijo el miércoles a Reuters que había recibido un correo electrónico que parecía proceder de Parker y en el que se le invitaba "a unirse a un nuevo proyecto sobre políticas de IA". Sin embargo, señaló que "le pareció un poco extraño, vagamente sospechoso" y, tras consultarlo con varios colegas, constató que era un impostor. Parker declaró a Reuters que Engler era una de las dos personas de las que tenía constancia que habían recibido mensajes sospechosos que supuestamente procedían de ella a principios de julio. Añadió que la acusación de implicación china tenía sentido. "Estados Unidos y China compiten en el ámbito de la IA", afirmó Parker. "Intentar que personas del ámbito de la política de IA revelen información sobre sus planes en materia de IA —si es que ese era realmente el objetivo— no es nada sorprendente".

item.title: Japón y Ecuador igualan sin goles en segundo encuentro de DT Gallardo al mando del combinado sudamericano
item.description: Las selecciones de fútbol de Japón y Ecuador igualaron sin goles el jueves, en un partido amistoso que se definió a favor del equipo japonés tras lanzamientos penales, en el segundo encuentro del argentino Marcelo Gallardo al mando del combinado sudamericano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las selecciones de fútbol de Japón y Ecuador igualaron sin goles el jueves, en un partido amistoso que se definió a favor del equipo japonés tras lanzamientos penales, en el segundo encuentro del argentino Marcelo Gallardo al mando del combinado sudamericano. Gallardo trató de corregir los errores comentidos por la selección en el primer partido de su era, que culminó con una categórica derrota de 3-0 a manos de Corea del Sur la semana pasada. Durante el partido, Ecuador tuvo más tiempo el balón con un juego con pases largos y por los extremos, pero no logró anotar. Gallardo realizó varios cambios en el medio campo para modificar el juego colectivo. Mientras, a Japón le faltó profundidad para complicar al arquero del equipo andino Hernán Galíndez, aunque aumentó la presión sobre la salida ecuatoriana en el segundo tiempo del encuentro, que se jugó en el Estadio Internacional de Yokohama. En la fase de penales, el arquero Zion Suzuki atajó un tiro del ecuatoriano Denil Castillo, dando el triunfo 5-4 a su equipo. Gallardo fue designado técnico de Ecuador el 13 de septiembre en sustitución de Sebastián Beccacece, quien en julio renunció tras perder por 2-0 ante México en los dieciseisavos de final de la reciente Copa del Mundo. El estratega argentino ha prometido trabajar para que la selección de fútbol dé un salto de calidad y tenga la convicción del potencial que tiene de cara al próximo Mundial.

item.title: Europe's defence spending props up shrinking refining sector, says VAROPreem CEO
item.description: Europe's shrinking oil refining sector is benefiting from rising demand for the fuel needed to support government defence plans, the CEO of one of the continent's biggest refiners said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Europe's shrinking oil refining sector is benefiting from rising demand for the fuel needed to support government defence plans, the CEO of one of the continent's biggest refiners said. European Union member states' defence spending rose for the 11th year running in 2025 to €418 billion ($472 billion), marking a 75% increase since 2021, with further gains forecast for this year, data from the European Council shows. "Every conversation I'm having with European governments today is all about how do you maintain resilience, how do you maintain continuity of supply? I would say that period between 2015 and 2022 the entire focus was how could you shut refineries down," VAROPreem CEO Dev Sanyal told Reuters on Thursday. "European governments realise that there's a need for more fuel. There's (also) a need for more energy because of the competitive advantage Europe wants to achieve on AI," he added. Since 2009, 30 of around 100 refineries operating in Europe have been closed or converted and at least seven converted into biorefineries, severely curbing the capacity to produce diesel, gasoline or jet fuel in the European Union, Britain, Norway and Switzerland, a report by trade group FuelsEurope said. "Now, with defence spending, you realise that whether you have F-35s (US-made fighter jets), you have Leopard tanks, they don't run on biogas," said the CEO of Swiss-headquartered VAROPreem, which has a capacity of around 530,000 barrels per day with refineries in Sweden, Switzerland and Germany. Refining capacity in EU countries, Britain, Turkey, Ukraine and Switzerland stood at 14.4 million bpd last year, down from 17.5 million bpd in 2009, according to the Statistical Review of World Energy most recently published by the Energy Institute. Diesel prices have rocketed since the Iran war choked off vital shipping lanes and following sustained attacks on Russian refining infrastructure. The benchmark European diesel futures contract has hit highs above $14 a metric ton since the Iran war began, levels last seen in the aftermath of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Meanwhile, US retail diesel prices hit a [USN:L6N45M0ZI TEXT:"record $6.50"] per gallon this month, with [USN:L6N45N0GM TEXT:"US pressure"] on Europe to release diesel stockpiles rising, sources said. ($1 = 0.8851 euros)

item.title: Netanyahu dice que el copiloto de flydubai fue sometido a un adoctrinamiento radical islamista
item.description: El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, afirmó el jueves que el copiloto que intentó estrellar un avión de pasajeros que se dirigía a Israel había sufrido un proceso de radicalización islamista.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, afirmó el jueves que el copiloto que intentó estrellar un avión de pasajeros que se dirigía a Israel había sufrido un proceso de radicalización islamista. "Sabemos que fue sometido a un adoctrinamiento radical islamista", declaró Netanyahu en una entrevista con Fox News. Aún no se ha determinado el motivo del angustioso incidente que estuvo a punto de provocar una catástrofe el miércoles en el vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai, que cubría la ruta de Dubái a Tel Aviv, en el que los pasajeros lograron reducir al agresor y la tripulación de reserva a bordo aterrizó el avión en Arabia Saudita . Netanyahu declaró en el programa Fox & Friends que en cuestión de días podría confirmar si el copiloto de flydubai tenía vínculos con Irán. "Creo que es demasiado pronto para decir si tenía alguna conexión con Irán o con cualquier otra persona", afirmó. Netanyahu señaló que estaba claro que el copiloto tenía tendencias suicidas. "Si a eso le sumamos lo que acabo de comentarles sobre las tendencias islamistas y la radicalización que se aprecian en sus antecedentes, creo que eso nos dará una pista bastante clara", señaló. "Pero, insisto, aún no saco conclusiones definitivas. No obstante, ésas son las indicaciones de las que disponemos por ahora".

item.title: Brazil laudably ups the ante on betting crackdowns
item.description: President Lula wants to ban some $7 bln of legal online gambling, seizing on populist backlash as he seeks reelection. Black markets are a problem, but less so than the associated health effects and societal costs. As awareness spreads, so will tougher policies and prohibitions.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Goldfarb
item.content:encoded: All politics is local, but gambling troubles are global. It’s what makes the bold decision by Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva to outlaw online betting so compelling. In a bid to help his reelection campaign, he seized on populist backlash and reversed himself just a few years after authorizing the addictive activity. In doing so, his country will accelerate worldwide policy conversations about a spreading health epidemic. Ballot boxes and stock markets provide early barometers. Brazilians, who will [USN:L1N45G04J TEXT:"cast their votes"] in a close race on Sunday, made their concerns clear: 75% of those polled recently backed an online betting ban. Local site operators, including Entain and Flutter Entertainment, will suffer from the license revocations in a promising $7 billion growth market . Allwyn scrapped its earlier profit margin guidance following the executive order. Lula’s radical course of action, which faces a legal challenge and requires congressional approval to stay in place, also speaks to otherwise tepid regulatory responses. It has been two years since an international panel convened by medical journal Lancet flagged that the damage to public health and wellbeing from gambling, including suicide and domestic violence, is “more substantial than previously understood.” Sophisticated marketing and betting on mobile phones are largely to blame. Popular prediction markets are also now feeding the frenzy. The industry’s main argument is that online wagering will simply wind up overseas or controlled by organized crime networks if governments don’t legalize it. There’s some basis for such theories, including Australia’s experience with high excise rates pushing tobacco trade onto the black market. Major inconvenience and risks of offshore options would dissuade many casual bettors, however. What’s more, stiff restrictions on advertising, sponsorship, game design, lending and stake limits would go a long way to protect users. In Britain, where gambling is deeply woven into the culture, new rules designed to fit the digital age, aim to stop companies from being allowed to put profit ahead of protection. As communities and politicians start to fully appreciate related financial and health repercussions, outright shutdowns like Brazil’s will garner greater consideration. Prohibition-era bootlegging continues to captivate the public imagination but often lost to collective memory is that temperance was a powerful political movement that overcame deep-pocketed distillers. Booze consumption, along with death rates from alcoholism and cirrhosis, declined steeply under the Volstead Act, and decades went by before they reached early-1900s levels again. Sweeping bans on betting remain a long-shot, but the odds just improved. Follow Jeffrey Goldfarb on X and Linkedin . Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on September 25 banned online betting as he campaigns for reelection in a tight race with opponent Flavio Bolsonaro. The executive order took effect immediately, but it must be approved by Congress within 120 days to stay in force. Lula signed legislation in 2023 establishing rules and explicitly authorizing online games in addition to sports betting. Licensed operators have been allowed to offer services nationwide since January 2025, after paying concession fees and meeting regulatory requirements. Although Brazil legalized online betting in 2018 under former President Michel Temer, it had remained largely unregulated. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Des frappes aériennes pakistanaises font neuf morts en Afghanistan, selon les taliban
item.description: Des frappes aériennes pakistanaises sur l'Afghanistan ont fait neuf morts jeudi, a déclaré le gouvernement taliban, tandis qu'Islamabad a affirmé avoir tué 22 "terroristes".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des frappes aériennes pakistanaises sur l'Afghanistan ont fait neuf morts jeudi, a déclaré le gouvernement taliban, tandis qu'Islamabad a affirmé avoir tué 22 "terroristes". Ces bombardements marquent une escalade dans les combats entre les deux pays voisins après trois mois de calme relatif. Parmi les personnes tuées lors des frappes menées dans les provinces afghanes de Kunar et d'Helmand figurent des femmes et des enfants, a déclaré le porte-parole des taliban, Zabihullah Mujahid, sur le réseau social X, ajoutant que 11 personnes avaient été blessées. "Nous condamnons cet acte, que nous qualifions d’agression et de crime en violation de tous les principes reconnus", a-t-il ajouté. La Mission d’assistance des Nations unies en Afghanistan (MANUA) a indiqué qu’au moins 10 civils avaient été tués lors de ces frappes, dont la plupart étaient des enfants, et que neuf autres avaient été blessés. Le ministère pakistanais de l’Information a déclaré que ces frappes reposaient sur des "renseignements fiables" et visaient des caches de "terroristes" dans deux endroits différents. "Les cibles ont été détruites avec précision et les premiers rapports font état de la mort de 22 terroristes", a-t-il indiqué dans un communiqué publié sur X. "De grandes quantités d’armes et de munitions stockées dans ces repaires ont également été détruites", a-t-il ajouté. Reuters n’a pu vérifier ces informations de manière indépendante. Une attaque menée par des hommes armés contre un poste de police dans le nord-ouest du Pakistan le mois dernier, qui a fait 24 morts, a ravivé les tensions entre le Pakistan et l’Afghanistan. Islamabad accuse Kaboul d’abriter des "terroristes" qui mènent des attaques transfrontalières. Le gouvernement taliban nie ces accusations et affirme que le terrorisme est un problème interne au Pakistan.

item.title: Apenas 13% das empresas avançam em IA diante de barreiras regulatórias e sistemas de TI antigos
item.description: Apenas 13% das empresas estavam no caminho certo com suas iniciativas de IA, já que obstáculos regulatórios e a integração com sistemas de TI antigos retardaram a adoção em larga escala, segundo um estudo da BearingPoint.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Apenas 13% das empresas estavam no caminho certo com suas iniciativas de IA, já que obstáculos regulatórios e a integração com sistemas de TI antigos retardaram a adoção em larga escala, segundo um estudo da BearingPoint. Quase três quartos das empresas pesquisadas relataram resultados financeiros positivos com a IA, mas menos de um terço conseguiu ir além dos projetos-piloto, informou a consultoria nesta quinta-feira. “A IA ultrapassou um limiar importante”, disse o especialista da BearingPoint, Frederic Gigant, acrescentando que comprovar o valor e ampliá-lo são duas coisas diferentes. Cerca de 40% dos entrevistados citaram as regulamentações legais como a principal barreira para a ampliação da IA, enquanto 34% apontaram os desafios de integrar a nova tecnologia aos sistemas de TI existentes. Perto de 24% das empresas relataram economias de custo impulsionadas pela IA de pelo menos 10%, em comparação com apenas 4% que relataram crescimento de receita na mesma proporção. Além disso, quase dois terços das empresas estimaram um excesso de pessoal de pelo menos 10%. A China e os EUA lideram a adoção da IA, com 20% e 18% das empresas relatando implementação abrangente, contra 8% na Alemanha. Já a proporção de empresas com IA profundamente integrada às operações subiu de 7% em 2025 para 11% em 2026.

item.title: Water contamination and cancer concerns
item.description: Hello!
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hello! Today’s newsletter highlights three separate stories from the United States, Madagascar and Cuba. They all have one thing in common - contamination. We’ll look at how Iowa's soaring cancer rates have become a campaign issue ahead of November’s midterm elections. Many voters fear that the state's worsening water pollution from nitrates and other chemicals may be to blame for a spike in cases. Then we’ll unpack a legal showdown pitting more than 6,500 people in Madagascar against mining group Rio Tinto. The islanders have filed a claim in London’s High Court, alleging that contamination from the company's mineral sands operation exposed them to dangerous levels of lead and uranium. Meanwhile, health authorities in Cuba have warned in recent days of the spread of viruses, including a strain of viral hepatitis, as power and water increasingly fail. * Cancer concerns and contaminated water Iowa's rising cancer rate - the second highest in the US behind Kentucky - has emerged as a major campaign issue ahead of this year’s vote. A Reuters review of campaign materials showed that every major candidate in Iowa's [USN:L4N42Y0N6 TEXT:"competitive races"] for Congress and the state governorship has talked about their plans to tackle cancer in speeches and online posts. Candidates have pledged a range of actions from increasing cancer screening to improving water quality monitoring. It is one of just three states where cases are rising, driven by higher rates of lung, prostate and breast cancers, among others, according to the National Cancer Institute at the National Institutes of Health. Many Iowans tie their cancer concerns to high nitrate levels in the state's water, which can occur when fertilizer washes into rivers and groundwater. About 85% of Iowa is farmland, much of it dedicated to fertilizer-heavy crops such as corn, according to the US Department of Agriculture. The concentration of nitrates in Iowa's main waterways doubled over the past 50 years and regularly exceeds levels set by the Environmental Protection Agency, according to a 2025 statewide report commissioned by Iowa's Polk County Board of Supervisors. Scientists have not reached a consensus on the cancer risk posed by nitrate-contaminated drinking water. Some studies, including by the University of Iowa and the National Cancer Institute, have found associations with higher cancer rates or mortality, while others have not. [USN:L6N44F10S TEXT:"Click here"] to find out more about Iowa’s cancer concerns and the possible links between the disease, contaminated water and pesticides. * Rio Tinto acidic wastewater case Over in Britain, a lawsuit has been brought by [USN:L1N45M0AS TEXT:"community groups from Madagascar"] who live near Rio Tinto's QIT Madagascar Minerals (QMM) mine. According to law firm Leigh Day, which is representing the claimants, the community groups allege that acidic wastewater containing uranium, lead and other metals was discharged into lakes and waterways used for drinking, cooking, washing and irrigation. The mine, which is 80%-owned by Rio Tinto, produces ilmenite, which is processed into titanium dioxide, a white pigment used in products including paint, food and toothpaste. Rio Tinto said it had been notified of the claim but had not yet received details, so could not comment further at the moment. * Clinics without water In Cuba, power outages exacerbated by a US oil blockade have crippled the already crumbling infrastructure that supplies water to Havana's nearly 2 million people. Many regularly go without running water for days or weeks. Healthcare worker Yuamilka Hechavarria told Reuters how she had been forced to buy water from street vendors or scavenge it from broken pipes. [USN:L1N45H0OH TEXT:"Click here"] for the full story to find out more about how local clinics are struggling to cope without water. * Talking Points Thailand floods: The [USN:L6N45L05A TEXT:"death toll from rains and flooding"] in Thailand rose to 23, authorities said, as waters receded from the hard-hit capital Bangkok. The city's governor, Chadchart Sittipunt, said he expected floodwater to drain away from major roads within two days, though it will take up to a week for other inundated areas to be cleared out. US climate litigation: Officials in Boulder, Colorado are seeking to hold major oil companies liable for helping drive climate change and misleading the public about the risks of fossil fuels in a Supreme Court case set to be argued on October 5. The case could determine the fate of dozens of climate-related lawsuits by state and local governments against fossil fuel companies. [USN:L1N45G0O2 TEXT:"Click here"] to learn more about their arguments. UK climate rollbacks: The [USN:L6N45M0QL TEXT:"Financial Conduct Authority"], Britain's financial regulator, has dropped plans to require listed companies to inform investors about their climate risks after firms raised concerns about implementation costs and competitiveness. The move follows steps by the European Union to water down its flagship corporate climate disclosure regime. EU methane rules: The European Commission is considering a postponement of the EU's methane emissions rules for oil and gas imports – set out in the world's first law targeting methane emissions from imported fossil fuels – after calls from France, the US and other governments that said the rules could undermine energy security. [USN:L8N45K07G TEXT:"Click here"] for an explainer on the rules. Ghana illegal mining crackdown: Ghana, Africa's biggest gold producer, has tightened oversight of its mining sector to boost revenue, increase local participation and strengthen compliance, a senior regulator said. [USN:L8N45J070 TEXT:"Click here"] to find out more about the mining companies that have been fined and investigated for environmental breaches and compliance issues linked to illegal gold mining activity. * ESG Spotlight Today’s spotlight showcases a British startup that is turning waste into fertilizer. Meet NPK Recovery , a company that collects urine from event toilets and processes it into a liquid fertilizer containing nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, using its "pee-cycle" technology. Today’s Sustainable Switch was edited by Andrew Heavens Think your friend or colleague should know about us? Forward this newsletter to them. They can also subscribe here.

item.title: La Russie expulse des diplomates hongrois en guise de représailles
item.description: La Russie prévoit d'expulser un nombre non précisé de diplomates hongrois, a déclaré jeudi le ministère des Affaires étrangères russe, une mesure de rétorsion en réponse à la décision prise le mois dernier par Budapest de renvoyer dix diplomates russes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Russie prévoit d'expulser un nombre non précisé de diplomates hongrois, a déclaré jeudi le ministère des Affaires étrangères russe, une mesure de rétorsion en réponse à la décision prise le mois dernier par Budapest de renvoyer dix diplomates russes. "À titre de mesure de rétorsion, un groupe de membres du personnel de l'ambassade de Hongrie à Moscou et des consulats généraux de Hongrie à Saint-Pétersbourg et à Kazan doit quitter le territoire de la Fédération de Russie dans un délai de deux semaines", a précisé le ministère. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères hongrois dit dans un communiqué prendre acte de la décision russe, ajoutant : "La Hongrie n'a aucun intérêt à voir s'aggraver les tensions diplomatiques". Budapest avait accusé les [USN:L8N45011O TEXT:"diplomates"] russes d'avoir agi d'une manière incompatible avec leur statut — une formulation souvent utilisée comme euphémisme pour désigner l'espionnage. Ces expulsions étaient la bonne illustration du revirement de la politique de la Hongrie vis-à-vis de la Russie depuis que l'ancien Premier ministre Viktor Orban a dû quitter le pouvoir en avril à la suite de sa défaite électorale aux législatives après 16 années à la tête du gouvernement. Malgré l'invasion à grande échelle de l'Ukraine par la Russie en février 2022, Viktor Orban s'était distingué au sein de l'Union européenne en continuant à entretenir des liens étroits avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine. La Hongrie a aussi continué à acheter du pétrole et du gaz russe, a entravé les sanctions européennes contre la Russie et a tenté de bloquer un prêt de 90 milliards d'euros de l'UE à l'Ukraine. Le nouveau chef du gouvernement hongrois, Peter Magyar, et ses ministres ne cessent de répéter que les principales alliances de la Hongrie sont nouées avec l'UE et l'Otan, deux institutions avec lesquelles ils entendent restaurer une confiance ébranlée sous Viktor Orban.

item.title: China driving worrying rise in EU imports, Commission official says
item.description: Nearly a quarter of imports into the European Union are rising at a "worrying" rate, driven primarily by goods from China, the European Commission's chief trade enforcement officer said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Philip Blenkinsop
item.content:encoded: Nearly a quarter of imports into the European Union are rising at a "worrying" rate, driven primarily by goods from China, the European Commission's chief trade enforcement officer said on Thursday. Denis Redonnet told the European Parliament that sectors facing sustained and abnormal import growth included machinery, textiles, basic metals and chemicals. Redonnet was addressing the parliament's trade committee as the Commission intensifies discussions with Beijing to address the EU's goods trade deficit with China of €360 billion ($407 billion) in 2025. Chinese imports into the bloc have been rising while EU exports to China have fallen by a similar rate, and Brussels [USN:S8N3US031 TEXT:"hopes to agree"] some form of Chinese export management this month. "It is of serious concern that the import surveillance or barometer results... show potentially worrying trends for almost a quarter of all imports into the EU at the moment," Redonnet said. "And China and Chinese origin is the main driver of these import increases." EU imports totalled €2.53 trillion ($2.86 trillion) in 2025, with €571 billion from China. The increased exports have driven a sharp increase in industry requests for trade defence measures. The EU executive Commission launched 32 new cases in 2025, just off the 2024 record of 33 and compared to a previous historical annual average of 12. More than a third of new investigations involved the chemicals sector. Redonnet said 27 new cases had already been opened in 2026. ($1 = 0.8854 euros)
